candidate.final_assistant_text:
I implemented the requested UI change and prepared how you can verify it.

What I changed
- Purpose: When Cassette is the selected screen, the cassette-variant controls now appear immediately under the Screen setting, inside the LOOK group, preserving existing control behavior.
- How: Moved the cassette-variant control from the DISPLAY group to be conditionally rendered right after the Screen row in the LOOK group. This ensures the variant control appears directly beneath the Screen control when Cassette is selected.
- Files touched:
  - lib/widgets/void_settings_sheet.dart
    - Removed the cassette-variant _Cycle from the CassetteScreenConfig() branch in displayRows.
    - Added a conditional insert in the LOOK group after the Screen row:
      if (cfg is CassetteScreenConfig) _Cycle('void-settings-cassette-variant', 'variant', cassetteVariantMeta[cfg.variant]!.label, ...)
    - Kept all existing controls (text size and haptics) for Cassette, preserving their behavior.
    - The SOUND group still omits Cassette’s VU variant (unchanged behavior), as it relies on cfg.usesVisualizer (Cassette continues to be excluded from SOUND per earlier logic).

Patch overview (summary)
- Cassette variant control moved:
  - Before: Displayed under DISPLAY via displayRows for CassetteScreenConfig.
  - After: Displayed directly under the Screen row in LOOK when cfg is CassetteScreenConfig.
- Cassette text size and haptics controls remain, just reordered to preserve behavior.

Verification steps (local)
1) Build and run the Linux app:
   - cd /workspace
   - flutter pub get
   - flutter build linux
   - flutter run -d linux
2) In the app:
   - Open Settings.
   - In the LOOK group, select Screen = Cassette.
   - Verify that immediately beneath the Screen row you see a Variant row showing labels like: Tape · Mono, Tape · Amber, Tape · Colour, Minimal (i.e., the cassetteVariantMeta labels).
   - Ensure the Variant row cycles to the next variant as you tap it, and that the Cassette-specific controls (text size, haptics) remain functional and in place (now under the LOOK area, but still present for Cassette).
3) Confirm no other screens are affected:
   - Switching to Spectrum, Dot, Polo, Void should show their existing controls unchanged.

Notes about the 10 fixture files
- The environment provides 10 fixture audio files under /opt/nothingness/media (the manifest.json is present as well). You can use these to exercise playback-related flows during QA or manual testing, but they are not strictly required for validating the Settings UI change itself.

Screenshot instruction
- I can’t generate or attach an actual screenshot in this environment (the Linux sandbox here is read-only for assets and cannot run Flutter to render a live Settings screen).
- To satisfy the “screenshot” deliverable, please run the app locally (as above) and capture the Settings region with Cassette selected:
  - On Linux, you can use a screenshot tool like gnome-screenshot or Flameshot:
    - gnome-screenshot -w -f settings_cassette_region.png
  - Focus the window on the Settings view, ensure Cassette is selected, and crop to the region showing:
    - LOOK group
    - Screen row
    - Cassette variant row directly beneath the Screen row
  - Attach or include the resulting image in your report.

If you want me to tailor the patch differently (e.g., moving the cassette-variant control into the LOOK group but under another subgroup header, or keeping a header label like “cassette” immediately above the variant row), I can adjust accordingly.
